disclosingAndReceiving: Kestrel Data Systems Ltd (synthetic, England, UK)

purpose: Evaluation of a potential data collaboration
forum: Courts located in New York County, New York

criteria.label: Agreement structure
criteria.note: Mutual, standalone NDA for a stated evaluation purpose.

criteria.label: Definition of confidential information
criteria.note: Captures all information of any kind, whether or not marked, including information that is or becomes public through no fault of the recipient.

criteria.label: Obligations of the receiving party
criteria.note: Reasonable care, purpose limitation and need-to-know disclosure.

criteria.label: Standard carveouts
criteria.note: Public knowledge, prior possession, third-party receipt and legal compulsion are present; independent development is missing.

criteria.label: Permitted disclosures
criteria.note: Employees, contractors, advisors and affiliates under similar obligations.

criteria.label: Term and duration
criteria.note: Three-year term is acceptable; confidentiality survives seven years, longer than the five-year default but within a common market range.

criteria.label: Return and destruction
criteria.note: Return or destroy on request; no retention exception for legal, regulatory or backup copies.

criteria.label: Remedies
criteria.note: Mutual injunctive-relief acknowledgment; no liquidated damages.

criteria.label: Problematic provisions
criteria.note: Twelve-month employee non-solicitation; broad residuals clause granting a perpetual licence to use retained information, including for the recipient's products.

criteria.label: Governing law and jurisdiction
criteria.note: New York law and New York courts; no mandatory arbitration.

redIssues.risk: Could capture public information and material independently developed by the recipient
redIssues.fix: Limit to non-public information disclosed for the purpose and identified as confidential, or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential; preserve the standard exclusions.

redIssues.risk: Claims that the recipient's products or features were derived from the discloser's information
redIssues.fix: Add a carveout for information independently developed without use of or reference to the confidential information.

redIssues.risk: Restricts ordinary hiring and does not belong in an NDA
redIssues.fix: Delete clause 6. If the counterparty insists, narrow it to targeted solicitation with a short term, subject to local law.

redIssues.risk: Effectively licenses the discloser's confidential information for the recipient's products
redIssues.fix: Delete clause 10. If retained, limit it to unaided memory, exclude trade secrets and patentable information, and grant no IP licence.

yellowIssues.risk: Longer than the stated five-year default
yellowIssues.fix: Confirm the business need; reduce to five years unless trade-secret protection justifies longer.

yellowIssues.risk: Conflicts with legal, regulatory or backup retention obligations
yellowIssues.fix: Add a retention exception for copies required by law, regulation or bona fide backup/compliance policy.

classificationRule: Any FAIL -> RED; otherwise any FLAG -> YELLOW; otherwise GREEN.
jurisdictionFlags: UK counterparty: UK GDPR may apply if personal data is shared; the NDA has no data-protection terms.
New York law and forum are stated consistently; no mandatory arbitration.
Non-solicitation enforceability varies by jurisdiction and should be reviewed locally.
No signature authority is established by the document; the organization's delegation policy governs.
